54M, EW EMER. admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to HOME HEALTH CARE
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Other ascites; Abdominal pain, other specified site; Rash and other nonspecific skin eruption
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Hepatic encephalopathy
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Hepatic encephalopathy; Pneumonia, organism unspecified; Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile; Hyposmolality and/or hyponatremia; Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver; Alcohol abuse, in remission; Other psoriasis; Mineral deficiency, not elsewhere classified; Depressive disorder, not elsewhere classified
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: none
PROCEDURES: Percutaneous abdominal drainage
MEDICATIONS: Benzonatate 100mg PO; Thiamine 100mg PO/NG; Furosemide 80mg PO/NG; MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) 500mg PO/NG; Lactulose 30mL PO/NG; Zinc Sulfate 220mg PO/NG; Albuterol 0.083% Neb Soln 1NEB IH; Potassium Chloride 40mEq PO; TraMADOL (Ultram) 50mg PO; Maalox/Lidocaine 5-10mL ORAL; Magnesium Oxide 400mg PO/NG; Bag 50mL IV; Magnesium Sulfate 2gm IV; Spironolactone 100mg PO/NG; Levofloxacin 750mg PO/NG; Heparin 5000UNIT SC; Albumin 25% (12.5g / 50mL) 50g IV; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3mL IV; traZODONE 12.5-25mg PO/NG; NS 100mL IV; Rifaximin 550mg PO/NG; Guaifenesin 5-10mL PO/NG; FoLIC Acid 1mg PO/NG; Multivitamins 1TAB PO/NG; Triamcinolone Acetonide 0.1% Ointment 1Appl TP
MICROBIOLOGY: STOOL: CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE
SERVICES: MED
WARDS: Emergency Department; Transplant
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 54-year-old male admitted from the Emergency Room.
[2] The patient presented with other ascites, abdominal pain, and rash and other nonspecific skin eruption.
[3] The primary diagnosis is Hepatic encephalopathy.
[4] The active diagnoses are Hepatic encephalopathy, Pneumonia, organism unspecified, Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile, Hyposmolality and/or hyponatremia, Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver, Alcohol abuse, in remission, Other psoriasis, Mineral deficiency, not elsewhere classified, and Depressive disorder, not elsewhere classified.
[5] The patient has no Past Medical History.
[6] The patient underwent Percutaneous abdominal drainage.
[7] The patient was treated with Benzonatate 100mg PO, Thiamine 100mg PO/NG, Furosemide 80mg PO/NG, MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) 500mg PO/NG, Lactulose 30mL PO/NG, Zinc Sulfate 220mg PO/NG, Albuterol 0.083% Neb Soln 1NEB IH, Potassium Chloride 40mEq PO, TraMADOL (Ultram) 50mg PO, Maalox/Lidocaine 5-10mL ORAL, Magnesium Oxide 400mg PO/NG, Bag 50mL IV, Magnesium Sulfate 2gm IV, Spironolactone 100mg PO/NG, Levofloxacin 750mg PO/NG, Heparin 5000UNIT SC, Albumin 25% (12.5g / 50mL) 50g IV, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3mL IV, traZODONE 12.5-25mg PO/NG, NS 100mL IV, Rifaximin 550mg PO/NG, Guaifenesin 5-10mL PO/NG, FoLIC Acid 1mg PO/NG, Multivitamins 1TAB PO/NG, and Triamcinolone Acetonide 0.1% Ointment 1Appl TP.
[8] The patient was cultured for STOOL: CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE, which was sensitive to MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) and resistant to Levofloxacin.
[9] The patient was evaluated by the MED service.
[10] The patient was admitted to the Emergency Department and Transplant wards.
[11] The patient was discharged alive to HOME HEALTH CARE.
